policy: Unpublished Snapshot v5 uses Starter openings and explicit Direct MCP server toolAccessMode ALL/ALLOWLIST and assistant mcpBindings with toolSelection ALL/ALLOWLIST; ALL follows dynamic discovery without reviewed-contract locking or additional invocation confirmation; tool selection is independent from explicit per-tool approvalPolicy, new editor grants default AUTO and existing policies are preserved; ALLOWLIST must be nonempty, allowedTools and toolNames are required, full Tool JCS contractHash and AUTO/REQUIRE_CONFIRMATION policy. v5 server-only assistant references are retired; missing tool fields require explicit draft authoring. Retained published v4 uses independent DTOs, original bytes/hash and republish recovery. API v1, Bridge v3, Relay workspace control protocol is v3; retained MCP usage targets remain v2, new DAV statistics-only targets use v3. Current v5 Android consumer verification is pending; Core-generated exports alone do not prove deployment compatibility. Gateway remains a separate later stage. Supported Client/Portal/Bridge response objects recursively ignore unknown fields; commands remain closed, known execution and permission semantics remain validated. Retained Snapshot v4/v5 original bytes/hash remain unchanged. New v5 optionally defines workspace-derived WebDAV resources; per-user workspace projection identifies the unique file exchange DAV and confirmed READ_ONLY/FULL permission. Platform Bearer DAV is transparently relayed using private explicit bindings, Activation-managed credentials and session-bounded streaming. Files remains available independently of DAV resource publication and is not metered; DAV records basic transport statistics without budget admission or billing. HTTP localhost/LAN endpoints are allowed. Explicit revocation is durable; an upstream 401 withdraws only its matching binding and never automatically overwrites an external key. Bridge capability advertisements tolerate unknown methods without enabling them and unknown error codes remain failures. Android source is outside this change and requires actual consumer verification. Admin release history supports bounded preview/execute cleanup and optional retention, protecting current control targets while keeping generation, usage, session and idempotency facts independent. Unpublished v5 assistant mcpBindings denote mandatory servers, not the exclusive enterprise server set. Enabled unbound enterprise MCP may be explicitly selected through existing per-user assistant usage preferences; mandatory tool restrictions take precedence over duplicate selection. Removing a binding removes its mandatory status and assistant restriction. Published v4 retains its original reference semantics. The MCP selection revision adds no product, platform-contract or Snapshot version; Android consumer implementation and verification remain pending.
